concepts.objective: Identify changes in the population, measurement or target-generating process and distinguish within-environment performance from evidence about deployment.
Distinguish prediction from intervention targets and explain why neither predictive strength nor a causal label alone guarantees robustness.
Compare conditional relationships across environments and state the mechanism and support assumptions needed for a scoped invariance argument, without treating stability as causal proof.
Design external-environment checks for prediction and generation, including content preservation, failure monitoring and abstention when evidence does not cover the intended use.

claims.proposition: A relationship useful for prediction in observed environments need not apply in a new environment whose generating processes or support differ.

source_refs.locator: Section 8.3, Domain Adaptation, environments and equation (8.7)

claims.proposition: The most informative observational predictor need not be an effective intervention target, because prediction and changing the target are different tasks.

source_refs.locator: Section 6.3, Example 6.10, Predictors and intervention targets

claims.proposition: Under a causal model, changes to other mechanisms can leave the target mechanism invariant. Domain generalization additionally assumes that the relevant conditional relationship persists in the test environment and has adequate support; stability can also occur for non-parent predictor sets.

source_refs.locator: Section 6.6, equation (6.7); Section 8.3, equation (8.7), discussion of non-parent sets and overlapping supports

claims.proposition: Evidence from multiple environments is interpreted under assumptions about which mechanisms change. Hidden variables and previously unexamined mechanism changes can invalidate an invariance argument.

source_refs.locator: Section 8.3, equation (8.7) assumptions; Section 9.5.6, restrictions on hidden variables and environment interventions

claims.proposition: Reference counts and assessment cases in this pack are authored teaching data. Interactive experiment outcomes are deterministically recomputed from the released model and learner settings. Ratios, differences and weighted sums use declared denominators and target weights. Generation fidelity and withholding criteria are declared teaching-model rules, not empirical guarantees or textbook claims about a particular generator.

resources.text: An assistant predicts whether reference inspection confirms parcel damage from parcel photographs and drafts a short report. Its old test score is high. What must be checked before moving it to another warehouse?
Worked example

Name the people or objects sampled, the input acquisition process, the endpoint definition and the intended use. In this case the new warehouse may have different case proportions, cameras or scanners, labels and reporting conventions. A familiar file format does not mean the generating process is unchanged.

The frequency of inputs can change while a useful target-given-input relation remains the same. Alternatively, measurement or the target-generating mechanism can change. A shift in warehouse-specific background label could break a shortcut; a change in reference labels could also change what success means. A lower score alone does not identify the cause.

A predictive score and a generated report are different outputs. Test prediction against independent reference outcomes; test generated content against source facts and required details. Use data from the intended external setting with a clean separation from training and tuning. A random split of the old setting does not recreate an unseen environment.

Distribution shift means that the joint data distribution differs between environments. Possible changes include case mixture, measurements, selection and the relation between inputs and the target; each has different implications.
Do not infer 'the model is robust' from a high score on another random subset of its original environment, or infer one causal explanation from a performance drop alone.
Specify which process could change, then collect evaluation evidence from the intended environment and output type.

External evaluation samples the intended changed setting. An old-environment split can measure a different question even when the input shape is identical; reference definitions and evaluation separation still need to be appropriate.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. External evaluation samples the intended changed setting. An old-environment split can measure a different question even when the input shape is identical; reference definitions and evaluation separation still need to be appropriate.
Which evidence includes the environment the model is actually expected to face?
A delivery predictor is trained and randomly split within City A. City B uses a different sensor protocol and has a different mix of routes. Which result directly addresses the proposed deployment?

External evaluation samples the intended changed setting. An old-environment split can measure a different question even when the input shape is identical; reference definitions and evaluation separation still need to be appropriate.

A shift can affect content grounding even if fluency is stable. This course's generation criterion separately checks preserved facts, critical omissions and unsupported additions in the target environment.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. A shift can affect content grounding even if fluency is stable. This course's generation criterion separately checks preserved facts, critical omissions and unsupported additions in the target environment.
A generator can produce convincing language while adding or omitting a crucial fact.

A product-description generator retains its old average language-quality score after a camera change, but no one has checked whether descriptions still match the photographed items and source records. What is missing?

A shift can affect content grounding even if fluency is stable. This course's generation criterion separately checks preserved facts, critical omissions and unsupported additions in the target environment.
Suppose the warehouse-specific background label predicts the target well in the original data. Would editing the marker change the underlying outcome? Would removing it guarantee a reliable model?
Worked example

Predicting whether reference inspection confirms parcel damage concerns an outcome from available inputs. Changing the true outcome is a different causal question. In the supplied case, editing an image marker changes the recorded input but does not change the underlying condition of the person or parcel.

The warehouse-specific background label might track which cases arrived at which warehouse. A model can exploit that association without learning the visible parcel condition. If the case mixture or marker convention changes, the shortcut can fail. Strong predictive association therefore does not establish a useful intervention on the underlying target.

A content-based or causally motivated feature still depends on measurement quality, available support and the target mechanism. A new low-light camera setup might obscure the feature. Test paired input perturbations and external outcomes; do not declare universal reliability merely because a feature has a plausible causal story.

Predictive usefulness concerns information about a target under a data distribution. Causal usefulness concerns what would change the target under an intervention. Robustness concerns performance over specified environment changes; none of these implies the others by itself.
Removing an obvious shortcut can help address one failure mode, but it does not prove the remaining model is causal or safe under every shift.
Ask separately: what predicts, what changes the outcome, and which environment changes the evidence covers.

The stipulated input edit does not change the underlying condition. It can reveal sensitivity to a cue but cannot establish a causal treatment effect; removing the cue also leaves other robustness questions open.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The stipulated input edit does not change the underlying condition. It can reveal sensitivity to a cue but cannot establish a causal treatment effect; removing the cue also leaves other robustness questions open.
Distinguish a change to a recorded cue from a change to the process producing the target.

A returns predictor relies on a warehouse label because that warehouse handles more fragile goods. In the declared case, digitally changing only that label leaves the parcel's condition unchanged. Which conclusion follows?

The stipulated input edit does not change the underlying condition. It can reveal sensitivity to a cue but cannot establish a causal treatment effect; removing the cue also leaves other robustness questions open.
Causal knowledge can motivate features and assumptions, but the model consumes measured values. Changed measurement, limited support and changes to the outcome mechanism can still cause failure.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. Causal knowledge can motivate features and assumptions, but the model consumes measured values. Changed measurement, limited support and changes to the outcome mechanism can still cause failure.
The mechanism and the way a feature is measured are separate parts of the system.

Traffic volume is genuinely upstream of journey time in the proposed transport model. The deployment city uses a new sensor that measures it poorly. Should 'causal feature' be treated as a guarantee of predictive robustness?
Causal knowledge can motivate features and assumptions, but the model consumes measured values. Changed measurement, limited support and changes to the outcome mechanism can still cause failure.
A content-based model performs similarly across three warehouses while a marker-based model varies sharply. What does that support, and what does it leave open?
Worked example

A shared aggregate accuracy is not the same as an invariant conditional relationship. Different subgroup errors can cancel in the average. Compare the outcome distribution given the candidate features across environments, using adequate sample sizes, common definitions and overlapping feature ranges.

A causal argument may suppose the rule linking the visible parcel condition to the reference target is unchanged, while the environment changes marker conventions or case mixture. Under such assumptions a target mechanism can remain stable. The argument fails if the new environment directly changes that target mechanism or destroys measurement of the relevant inputs.

Stable conditional patterns across observed environments support a candidate relation under stated assumptions, but do not uniquely prove its causal direction. Other predictor sets can be invariant too. A new environment outside the tested range needs new justification and evaluation, even if the old comparisons looked reassuring.

Invariance is the persistence of a specified relationship across specified environments. Domain generalization uses an assumption about persistence into an unseen setting, with adequate support; observing stability is evidence about that assumption, not a universal guarantee.
Equal overall scores can hide different conditional errors. Invariance across three sites does not prove the true graph or cover arbitrary interventions on the target.
State the conditional relationship, the changes already tested and which mechanism is assumed to remain fixed next.

The observed stability can support further investigation and a bounded prediction strategy. It neither uniquely establishes causality nor proves that an unseen target mechanism or measurement process will remain unchanged.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The observed stability can support further investigation and a bounded prediction strategy. It neither uniquely establishes causality nor proves that an unseen target mechanism or measurement process will remain unchanged.
Evidence across environments is useful without proving every causal or future claim.
Across three factories, the conditional relation between a candidate measured feature and the reference outcome looks stable over overlapping ranges. What is a justified interpretation?

The observed stability can support further investigation and a bounded prediction strategy. It neither uniquely establishes causality nor proves that an unseen target mechanism or measurement process will remain unchanged.
Marginal performance pools cases with different feature values. Conditional stability requires more targeted comparisons; equal overall scores alone do not supply that evidence.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. Marginal performance pools cases with different feature values. Conditional stability requires more targeted comparisons; equal overall scores alone do not supply that evidence.
The same average can result from different mixtures of different error rates.

Two towns both report 85% overall accuracy. One model misses many remote-route delays in Town B but few in A; the proportions of route types differ. Does equal overall accuracy establish invariance of the relevant conditional relation?
Marginal performance pools cases with different feature values. Conditional stability requires more targeted comparisons; equal overall scores alone do not supply that evidence.
The assistant now moves to a warehouse using a new low-light camera setup. It also generates reports. What evidence would make its limits visible before routine use?
Worked example

For prediction, choose the target label, useful error measures, important subgroups and uncertainty summaries. For generation, declare which input facts must be preserved, which unsupported additions are unacceptable and when a draft should be withheld for review. A fluent report can be wrong; an accurate average can conceal harmful subgroup errors.

Use an external-environment set separated from training and tuning. Review generated outputs against source records and an appropriate independent reference; compare omission and addition rates as well as language quality. Evaluate unsupported input ranges explicitly rather than letting the easy cases dominate the score.

If an input is outside evaluated support or the source cannot establish a required fact, abstain from a confident prediction or generated claim and route for review. Monitor drift and errors after any bounded use, and re-evaluate when conditions change. These checks reduce exposure to known gaps; they do not promise zero errors or universal robustness.

A robustness claim should name the output task, evaluated environments, metrics and remaining assumptions. For this course's generated reports, fidelity means preserving required source facts while avoiding unsupported additions, even when style changes.
A realistic-looking image, fluent paragraph or stable mean score does not establish factual preservation. Abstention is useful only with an explicit trigger and a practical review path.
Validate the intended setting, preserve the required content and define when the system must withhold an unsupported output.
The declared generation task permits changes of wording, not an inversion of the source fact. Fidelity must be evaluated separately from fluency or realism in the intended environment.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The declared generation task permits changes of wording, not an inversion of the source fact. Fidelity must be evaluated separately from fluency or realism in the intended environment.
Compare the meaning of the source assertion with the generated assertion.
An inspection-summary generator changes 'no crack found' to 'crack present' while adapting to a new factory's style. The paragraph is fluent and its style score improves. What has the output failed?
The declared generation task permits changes of wording, not an inversion of the source fact. Fidelity must be evaluated separately from fluency or realism in the intended environment.

The case exceeds evaluated support and lacks a required source fact. A declared abstention/review rule keeps an unsupported assertion from being presented as established; additional evaluation is needed before widening scope.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. The case exceeds evaluated support and lacks a required source fact. A declared abstention/review rule keeps an unsupported assertion from being presented as established; additional evaluation is needed before widening scope.
A missing source fact cannot be established by making the output sound confident.

An assistant receives a photograph from a new sensor outside its evaluated range, and the source is insufficient to determine the requested damage detail. Which operating rule best matches the evidence?

The case exceeds evaluated support and lacks a required source fact. A declared abstention/review rule keeps an unsupported assertion from being presented as established; additional evaluation is needed before widening scope.

A controlled environment comparison measures the selected model under the declared change. Its scope is the settings and outputs evaluated; neither an old score nor a model label guarantees performance under other measurement or target changes.

Reconsider the distinction in this case. A controlled environment comparison measures the selected model under the declared change. Its scope is the settings and outputs evaluated; neither an old score nor a model label guarantees performance under other measurement or target changes.
Compare evidence from the settings actually run, rather than extending a score to untested changes.

Keep the cue predictor, measurement error and generation strategy fixed. Submit a prediction and run with cue reliability at 90%. Change only cue reliability to 50%, predict again and run. Inspect the generated cases and compare prediction against reference truth. Reflect on which input relationship changed, what the scores show and how you revise your expectation for a new environment.

A change in a model's output is not necessarily a change in the real target.

Use the cue predictor and grounded generation. Hold cue reliability and measurement error fixed. Predict and run with cue editing off, then turn only cue editing on, make a new prediction and run again. Compare matching case IDs: source content and reference truth versus cue and prediction. Reflect on whether an input edit and an intervention on the underlying outcome are the same action.

Choose the content predictor and grounded generation. Predict and run the initial setting. Change only cue reliability, predict and run again; compare the reference groups and matching case IDs. You can then add a third run changing only measurement error to test a different boundary. Reflect on the relationship that stayed stable, which changes were actually tested and why this does not prove universal robustness.

Content fidelity concerns preservation of the measured source and its available context, while prediction accuracy concerns reference truth. Source-preserving generation may withhold an incomplete report; filling a gap does not establish its truth. Compare coverage, source fidelity and unsupported details from your runs before deciding how to review unsupported cases.

Evaluate predictions against independent reference truth and generated assertions against what the source actually contains.

Submit a prediction and run fluent generation, then change only the generator to grounded, predict and run again. Compare actual source text, report text, output coverage, source-fidelity metrics and prediction against reference truth. choices.text: Evaluation on appropriately labelled, held-out data from the intended new environment, with its measurement and population differences documented.
Another random split of the original environment, treated as a guarantee about the new setting.
Checking only that the input files have the same extension.
Nothing: a stable language score proves every generated factual statement remains correct.
External-setting content-fidelity evaluation against the source and relevant reference facts; fluent wording alone does not establish correct generation.
Only a prettier output font; output truth is unrelated to the changed inputs.
Because the marker predicts well, editing it must improve the underlying outcome.
Once the marker is removed, all future performance is guaranteed.
The marker can predict the outcome without being a lever that changes the underlying outcome.
No. A causal role does not repair measurement error, changed support or a changed target mechanism; evaluate the intended measurement process and environment.
Yes. Any genuinely causal feature is perfectly measured and invariant under every possible change.
No. A causal feature can never provide useful predictive information.
It proves this feature is a cause and guarantees accuracy after every future mechanism change.
It supports a scoped candidate invariance argument; causal interpretation and transfer still depend on assumptions about mechanisms, measurement and the new environment.
It has no relevance because only the best-fitting single site can matter.
Yes. Identical aggregate accuracy proves all mechanisms and subgroup errors are unchanged.
Yes. Subgroup composition never affects an aggregate performance score.
No. Aggregate equality can hide compensating subgroup errors; compare the relevant conditional behaviour with overlapping support and uncertainty.
Content preservation: the generated factual assertion contradicts the source, regardless of its fluent style.
Nothing: a better style score authorizes changing facts.
Only spelling; factual preservation is irrelevant to generation.
Generate the most plausible detail so the report is complete, then treat it as source evidence.
Flag the unsupported case, withhold the confident claim and request review or suitable reference information before extending the claimed scope.
Use the old mean score as a guarantee for the unsupported case.
A high score in the first run guarantees the same accuracy for every other environment.
The model with the most promising name is guaranteed robust without running the changed setting.
How the chosen predictor performs under these declared environment settings; an old score alone does not establish performance after a new change.
